html:
SMTO-GML-0039 — Gmail took too long to respond

GUID: b2158b03-a399-458d-b4dd-3de451a78d49
Slug: gmail-provider-timeout
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO waited for Google, but Gmail didn't answer in time, so the request stopped. If it was a send or a change, it may or may not have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running SMTO is connected to the internet and that Gmail opens quickly in a browser there. The request travels from the SMTO server to Google, so a slow or broken connection there causes this.
  2. If the Task was sending or changing email, check Sent, Drafts or Trash in Gmail before asking again. Google may have finished the change even though SMTO stopped waiting.
  3. Ask SMTO again with a smaller request, such as fewer emails or a shorter date range, and only for what is still missing. Smaller requests finish sooner and are less likely to run out of time.

What success looks like

  • SMTO returns the Gmail results, and any send or change appears in Gmail only once.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking again. Then select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO so they can check the server's connection to Google. Changing model or response time limits in Settings won't fix this, and don't resend email without checking Sent first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gmail API or Google OAuth request raised TimeoutError before completing; the REST client uses a 45-second socket timeout, and app-password accounts use the profile's timeout_seconds.

What this means

  • The native capability catches TimeoutError on the provider path after uncertain mutations have been handled separately. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • The native capability catches TimeoutError on the provider path after uncertain mutations have been handled separately.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect endpoint/route and retained operation stage; model generation timeout settings do not govern this transport.

How to fix it

  • Check DNS, proxy and network routing from the Server (or the paired Gateway for app-password accounts) to gmail.googleapis.com and oauth2.googleapis.com; model generation timeout settings do not control this request. For app-password accounts, timeout_seconds (1–120) in the profile can be raised. Before repeating any write, inspect the live mailbox to establish whether it was applied.
  • Check the Google endpoint and network route. Inspect current provider state before repeating a write; use the supported request flow once availability is restored. Model generation timeout settings do not control this request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported provider access completes within its actual timeout and original effects are known.

What not to do

  • Do not use a rapid retry loop or replay an uncertain mutation while waiting for the stated condition.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
